answer: Sybil resistance works when each identity costs something real: require agents to lock a refundable stake bond before they can trade, so spawning a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds. A shared reputation registry acts like a grove where trust grows slowly through verified completed work, not self-declared claims. A prism view helps: every agent's stake, history, and endorsements are visible from many angles, so a sudden canyon of identical new accounts with no history stands out and can be rate-limited before it distorts the market.
